state.context:
Review an ownership-syntax change for canlang, an AI-authored CRUD company-SaaS DSL. Adoption, economical source tokens, reliable generation and one canonical form per primitive are requirements. The user asks to research, validate, stop on an invalid proposal, brainstorm, consolidate, plan and implement this bounded default change. There are 44 .can sources: 46 explicitly team-scoped stored models, 67 roles all declaring in=team, and 116 explicit parent-contained models. No existing bare or app-scoped stored declarations were found. V1 roles only support team scope. The compiler, parser and runtime do not exist, so evidence is specification/source inspection, not executed authorization or tokenizer measurement.
Current rules require Model in team, Model in Parent or Model in app, and role Name in=team. Consider defaulting stored model declarations in Given to team via Model {...}, keeping containment and app scope explicit, and using role Name for the existing team role. Export status, package-qualified identities, owner-managed assignment and all stored fields remain. Model at=Binding {...} has default team scope plus its explicit storage placement; storage authority is independent of ownership. The default is a language-version rule, not package configuration, import context, surrounding model, filename or nearest app inference. The selected deployment app supplies the same team resolution as before; nothing creates a team when context is missing. Public record access resolves its team from the record as already specified; trusted operations still derive team from verified occurrences.
No permission is inferred: absent read policies deny, by/on authority stays explicit, and membership, field grants, references, invariants, uniqueness, locks and operation admission remain. Typed model-reference fields do not imply containment. Parent models still inherit protected parent/team/storage identity. Contracts, events, capability payloads, fixtures and struct/constructor expressions are not stored declarations and acquire no team owner. Declaring a role neither assigns it nor merges same-named package roles. Omission never selects app-wide scope. Removing only the 113 explicit team qualifiers from current sources should retain chosen effective scopes, policies, examples and all other text. The proposed canonical default grammar rejects redundant in team and role in=team with a correction diagnostic; unsupported role scopes stay errors. This requires a deliberate source migration and a specification update, including replacing the current No omitted ownership rule.
Benefits and tradeoffs: both defaults remove uniform repeated scope tokens but a mistakenly omitted child/app scope would become a valid team model, and readers/agents must learn this default. Keeping explicit model scope makes ownership visible and missing-scope declarations errors, at the cost of repeated tokens. Removing role scope alone saves its redundant qualifier while keeping model ownership visible, but retains substantial model boilerplate. Deferring allows executable parser/runtime evidence before grammar revision, but postpones a sourced repetition improvement. No option proves adoption or safety from corpus counts. OWASP recommends denying access without a grant and checking permissions on every request. PostgreSQL documents row-security enforcement separately from table declaration, including denial without a matching policy once enabled. Those are supporting authorization principles, not evidence that D1 provides PostgreSQL RLS or that this draft runtime enforces them. Assess the concrete rule set for contradictions as well as selecting a direction.

criteria.both_defaults: Adopt bare team models and bare team roles; retain explicit parent/app exceptions and reject repeated default qualifiers.
criteria.roles_only: Remove in=team from roles but keep explicit team/parent/app ownership on models.
criteria.explicit: Preserve the existing explicit model scopes and team-role qualifier for visible boundaries.
criteria.defer: Leave current source grammar pending executable evidence about the proposed ownership default.

preservation.instructions: Does the supplied default-and-migration contract preserve effective ownership, role identity and authorization for the illustrated cases without a concrete conflicting rule?
